title: Register tables get TWO conflicting mobile treatments (card-conversion vs shell scroll-table) that fight in Mobile mode
location: stock.html @media(max-width:640px) lines 397-413 (.rtbl card conversion) vs shell MOBILE_CSS index.html:6202-6208 (html.bcc-mobile[data-mod="stock"] .rtbl ...)
description: The module's own @media(max-width:640px) block turns every .rtbl register into stacked cards (.rtbl{display:block}, thead/tfoot{display:none}, tbody tr{display:block; card box}, td{display:flex;justify-content:space-between} with td::before{content:attr(data-label)}). The shell's per-module block instead treats .rtbl as a horizontally-scrolling TABLE and sizes its cells/inputs (.rtbl{font-size:11px!important}, .rtbl thead th{font-size:9px!important}, .rtbl td .ni{width:48px!important;min-height:0!important}). In Mobile mode at width <=640 BOTH fire simultaneously: the card layout renders, but the shell's higher-specificity input rules (html.bcc-mobile[data-mod=stock] .rtbl td .ni = (0,4,2)) override the card rule (.rtbl tbody td input = (0,1,3)), forcing inputs back to a fixed 48/80px box with min-height:0 instead of the card rule's flex:1 1 auto / min-height:40px. Net: inputs sit as narrow right-aligned boxes and lose their intended full-width touch sizing inside the card row.
impact: In the primary Mobile display at phone widths the data-entry inputs in Opening/Movements/Closing cards are cramped fixed-width boxes rather than the intended comfortable card fields; two layout systems partially cancel. Functional but visibly inconsistent and hard to tap accurately.
fix_hint: Decide ONE mobile treatment for .rtbl. Since the module already ships a full card conversion at <=640, gate the shell's stock .rtbl scroll-table rules so they do NOT set td-input width/min-height when the card layout is active (e.g. drop the .ni/.si/.cro-sel width+min-height:0 overrides from the shell stock block, or scope them to a non-card wrapper). Keep changes additive in the shell MOBILE_CSS string only.
evidence: MODULE: `.rtbl tbody td input, .rtbl tbody td select, .rtbl tbody td textarea { flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; width: auto !important; min-height: 40px; text-align: right; }`  SHELL: `html.bcc-mobile[data-mod="stock"] .rtbl td .ni{width:48px !important;min-height:0 !important;font-size:11px !important}`

title: In-table number inputs fall below the 44px tap floor in Mobile mode (shell stock override sets min-height:0 !important)
location: shell MOBILE_CSS index.html:6207-6208 (html.bcc-mobile[data-mod="stock"] .rtbl td .ni / .si / .cro-sel min-height:0 !important)
description: The global control floor html body input{min-height:44px !important} (index.html:6141-6151, specificity (0,0,3)) is meant to guarantee 44px tap targets. The shell's stock override html.bcc-mobile[data-mod="stock"] .rtbl td .ni{min-height:0 !important} has specificity (0,4,2) and WINS, so the number/select inputs inside register cells collapse to their padding height (~28-30px) in Mobile mode. The module's own card rule wanted min-height:40px, but as shown in stock-L01 the shell rule also beats that. Result: sub-44px controls in the densest, most-tapped part of the app.
impact: Physical-count/movement entry inputs are shorter than the accessibility tap floor on phones; more mis-taps during the core daily-count flow. Width-independent in Mobile mode (also affects the 1280xMobile mismatch).
fix_hint: Raise the shell stock override to min-height:40px (or drop min-height:0 so the 44px floor applies) for .rtbl td .ni/.si/.cro-sel; the 48/80px width caps can stay. Shell-only additive edit.
evidence: `html.bcc-mobile[data-mod="stock"] .rtbl td .ni{width:48px !important;min-height:0 !important;font-size:11px !important}` overrides `html body input:not([type=hidden])...{min-height:44px !important}`

title: Modal box has no max-height / internal scroll — tall modal on a short viewport can push footer buttons off-screen
location: stock.html .modal-box lines 299 & 388-391 (@640) — no max-height, no overflow
description: .modal-box sets min-width/max-width and padding but never max-height or overflow-y. .modal-overlay is display:flex;align-items:center. The two shipped modals (SM Login #sm-auth-modal, Delete-confirm #del-confirm-modal) are short, so today they fit. But the pattern is unsafe: on a landscape phone or with a large system font, a centered modal taller than the viewport is clipped top and bottom with NO way to scroll to the footer buttons (Login/Cancel, Delete/Cancel). The mobile keyboard opening on the password/DELETE input further shrinks the usable height.
impact: Edge-case only for the current two modals (both short), but a real risk when the keyboard is up on a small landscape screen: the action buttons can sit below the fold with no scroll. Low likelihood today, hence P2.
fix_hint: Add max-height:calc(100vh - 28px);overflow-y:auto to .modal-box (module CSS, additive) so any modal internally scrolls and its footer stays reachable. Purely presentational.
evidence: `.modal-box { background: var(--paper); border-radius: var(--radius-lg); padding: 28px 28px 24px; min-width: 300px; max-width: 400px; ... }` and @640 `.modal-box { min-width: 0; width: 100%; max-width: 420px; padding: 22px 18px 18px; }` — neither sets max-height/overflow.

title: Floor gate uses the FIRST same-day grooming record, not the latest — 2-per-day design + bus dedup desync
location: integration-bridge.js produce() lines 110-111 (emit id = d+':'+kk(r.name)); consumed by computeGate() L282-283. Root cause is grooming.html allowing 2 records/day (saveCRO gate L706 blocks only at >=2)
description: Grooming explicitly permits up to 2 records per CRO per day (saveCRO L706). The bridge producer emits GROOMING_RESULT with idempotency id `date:name`, so for a given CRO+day only the FIRST record ever emitted reaches the bus; the second is deduped and dropped (emit() L83-94 dedups on type:id, full scan). computeGate (L282) then blocks/clears using that first record's pct. Concrete failing sequence: CRO fails at 40% on the morning check (blocked from floor), then re-checks and passes at 100% later the same day — the 100% record is never emitted, so the gate keeps the CRO BLOCKED all day despite the corrected 100% record. The reverse also holds: pass first (100%) then a later 40% record is ignored and the CRO stays cleared.
impact: Cross-module floor-gate decision (QMS/DSR block banner) is driven by a stale grooming score whenever a CRO has 2 records the same day. A remediated CRO stays wrongly blocked, or a failing re-check is wrongly cleared. Silent — no error surfaces.
fix_hint: This fix belongs in integration-bridge.js (not editable per grooming scope): make the grooming producer emit the AGGREGATE/latest per name/day (e.g. include a record-count or max/last pct in the id, or emit id `date:name:idx` and have computeGate reduce to the latest/lowest per name). Flagging here because grooming's 2-per-day rule is what exposes it; grooming.html itself cannot fix it.
evidence: produce L111: emit(bus,'GROOMING_RESULT',d+':'+kk(r.name),{...pct...}); emit() L85-86 dedups on id → 2nd same-day record never emitted; computeGate L282-283 keys off e.payload.date===d and p.pct.

title: Locked-run snapshot keyed by empId||name collapses duplicate employees → wrong frozen pay shown to owner
location: payroll.html lockRun() line 3011 (snapshot[empKeyOf(row)]=calcGM(row)); consumed by gmComputed() lines 1730-1737 and empKeyOf() line 1693
description: lockRun() builds the frozen snapshot as an object keyed by empKeyOf(row) = String(row.empId||row.name).trim().toLowerCase(). Two GM employees can legitimately share that key: (a) same Emp ID typed twice (the module KNOWS this happens — checkGlobalValidation() line 1915-1916 emits a 'Duplicate Employee ID' WARNING, not a blocking error, and lockRun only blocks on slipRecords err-status, not on duplicate keys), or (b) two blank-empId rows with the same name, or (c) two rows with blank empId AND blank name (key=''). On lock, the second row overwrites the first in snapshot{}. After locking, gmComputed() serves run.snapshot[empKeyOf(row)] for BOTH rows, so both employees display the SECOND employee's salary/net/advance in the Saagar Traders sheet, Approval table, Salary Slips, Reports and every PDF. Concrete repro: two employees both with Emp ID 'E1' (or both blank), different gross; lock the run; both slips/register rows now show identical pay = the second one's. Owner pays and files statutory returns off wrong per-employee figures. Also advRecovered is keyed by voucher id so it survives, but the per-employee snapshot money is corrupted.
impact: Wrong money figure shown (and paid/filed) for one of two same-keyed employees in every locked view/PDF; silent, only visible if the owner cross-checks names. Data-integrity loss on the frozen pay-run.
fix_hint: Before locking, detect snapshot-key collisions among gmRows() (duplicate empKeyOf, including empty keys) and treat them as a BLOCKING error in runBlockingErrors()/lockRun() with a clear 'two employees share ID/blank identity — give each a unique Emp ID' message. Alternatively key the snapshot by a guaranteed-unique id (row.id when non-zero, else global index) instead of empId||name — but gmComputed lookup must use the same key, and note row.id can be 0 for legacy rows (see normalizeRow line 1567 / slipRecords comment lines 2332-2334, which already avoided row.id for exactly this reason).

title: Advance mid-month import Absent proposal caps at today's date only when payroll month == real calendar month → date-boundary mis-proration
location: payroll.html attFeedDiff() lines 3149-3164 (out.baseDays and prop.absent)
description: attFeedDiff() computes baseDays = (fk===curFk) ? Math.min(td, now.getDate()) : td, where fk is the PAYROLL month key (attFeedKey from state.meta.month/year) and curFk is the REAL calendar month (new Date()). Proposed Absent = max(0, baseDays − present − leave − half). The intent (comment lines 3138-3143) is to avoid marking every not-yet-elapsed day absent for the in-progress current month. But the gate is month-equality only. Failure cases: (1) Payroll is being run for the PREVIOUS month (very common — you close Jan payroll in early Feb): fk='2026-01' != curFk='2026-02', so baseDays=td=31 and Absent is correctly full-month — OK. (2) But if the user leaves state.meta.month on the current calendar month while the DSR feed is still sparse (feed only has the first few days), importing marks the rest of the month Absent unless it happens to be the same calendar month AND now.getDate() luckily matches — and Math.min(td, now.getDate()) uses getDate() (calendar day 1-31) against td which is a WORKING-days count net of holidays, so on a month with holidays baseDays can exceed the true elapsed working days, over-counting Absent. (3) Around the 00:30 new-day rule: now.getDate() flips at real local midnight, not at the app's ~00:30 boundary, so an import run between 00:00 and 00:30 uses the NEW day number while entries are still filed under the previous local date — off-by-one elapsed day in the Absent proposal.
impact: Imported Absent days (hence salary days and net pay) can be over- or under-stated by 1+ day for the in-progress month; a maker who trusts the diff and locks propagates the error to pay. Workaroundable: the maker reviews the diff and can hand-edit, so not silent data loss.
fix_hint: Base the elapsed-day cap on elapsed WORKING days (respecting holidays) rather than calendar getDate(), and derive 'today' from the same local-date key the rest of the app files entries under (stRealToday()/the app's 00:30 rule) rather than raw new Date().getDate(). Consider caching a stable 'as-of' day at import time so a cross-midnight import is deterministic.
evidence: const now=new Date(); const curFk=now.getFullYear()+"-"+String(now.getMonth()+1).padStart(2,"0"); out.baseDays=(fk===curFk)?Math.min(td,now.getDate()):td;  ... absent:Math.max(0,roundHalf(out.baseDays-safeN(f.present)-safeN(f.leave)-safeN(f.half)))

title: closeMonth into an already-locked target month silently downgrades that month's lock to draft, keeping a stale snapshot
location: payroll.html closeMonth() lines 3031-3045, esp. line 3041 ensureRun(curKey()).status="draft";
description: closeMonth() advances state.meta.month/year to the next month, then does ensureRun(curKey()).status="draft". ensureRun (line 2849) returns the EXISTING run object if one exists. If the target next month was previously locked (e.g. the user closed forward, later Unlocked+re-navigated, or navigated back and re-closed), that run already has status='locked' with a frozen snapshot and advRecovered. closeMonth flips only .status to 'draft' but LEAVES run.snapshot and run.advRecovered in place. Now: gmComputed() (line 1732 checks run.status==="locked") no longer serves the snapshot, so figures recompute live — but archiveKeys()/renderArchive still won't list it (status!=='locked'), AND advRecoveredBefore() (line 1703 requires status==='locked') stops counting that month's already-recorded advance recoveries, so vouchers can be re-scheduled/double-recovered in later months. The month's approver/lockedAt/formulaVersion metadata is also silently retained on a now-'draft' run. There is no confirm about clobbering an existing locked run for the target month.
impact: A previously-locked month can be silently un-locked (audit trail + frozen figures lost) and its advance recoveries stop counting, letting the same advance be recovered again downstream. Rare (requires navigating/closing into a month that already has a locked run) but corrupts money + audit state.
fix_hint: In closeMonth(), if the target month's run already exists with status==='locked', refuse or require an explicit unlock-first confirmation instead of blindly setting status='draft'. When intentionally resetting to draft, also clear/relocate snapshot and advRecovered so advRecoveredBefore stays consistent.

title: advVoucherNo() derives voucher number from array length → duplicate voucher numbers after any deletion

title: Leaves/agendas dated before May 2026 are unreachable and unreportable, yet an April-2026 leave still inflates the FY balance shown to the owner
location: prevMonth() line 1232-1233 + buildMonthJumper() line 1419-1434 (hard floor START_MONTH=4/START_YEAR=2026); fyUsage() line 939-951; openReport() per-month scan line 2104-2118
description: Calendar navigation and the month jumper are hard-floored at May 2026. importJSON()/isValidDateKey() accept ANY valid non-weekend date, so a backup can inject leaves for e.g. April 2026 or earlier. Those rows can never be shown on the grid (prevMonth() returns early at the floor and buildMonthJumper() starts at the floor) and never appear in the monthly report (openReport scans only the currently-viewed month). However fyRangeOf()/fyUsage() window the Indian FY as April-1→March-31, so an April-2026 approved leave IS inside FY2026-27 and is summed into the 'used X of Y this FY' figure shown in the Add-Leave balance hint (line 1765) and the report's FY Balance column (line 2162).
impact: Owner sees an FY leave-balance 'used' figure (e.g. 'Casual Leave: used 3 of 12') that includes leave days they cannot see, locate, or delete anywhere in the UI. The only remedy is Clear All. Confusing balance discrepancy; possible over-count of an employee's consumed quota with no visible source row.
fix_hint: Either (a) reject import date-keys earlier than the START_YEAR/START_MONTH floor in importJSON (add `if(k < dateKey(START_YEAR,START_MONTH,1)) {skipped++; return;}` alongside the existing weekend/validity checks), so no unreachable rows can be created; or (b) let prevMonth()/buildMonthJumper() extend back to the earliest date-key actually present in data.leaves/data.agendas so any stored leave is reachable and deletable. Additive/localStorage-safe.
evidence: prevMonth() line 1233 `if(currentYear===START_YEAR&&currentMonth===START_MONTH) return;`; buildMonthJumper() line 1423 starts at `y=START_YEAR,m=START_MONTH`; fyRangeOf() line 934 sets from `${s}-04-01` where s=year for month>=3, so April is in-FY; fyUsage() line 942 only filters by the FY window, not by the navigable range.

title: Approved leave dated more than 7 days in the past never reaches payroll (LEAVE_APPROVED never emitted for it)
location: integration-bridge.js produce() line 136 `if(String(dk).slice(0,10)<rc) return;` (rc=cutoffIso(RECENT_DAYS=7)); leave.html decideLeave() line 1011-1027 sets status='approved' with no re-emit path
description: The bridge producer only scans leave date-keys within RECENT_DAYS (7) of today when emitting LEAVE_APPROVED. A leave whose DATE is older than 7 days — a back-dated leave imported/created for last month, or a leave the owner approves late (the Approvals modal at line 796-800 explicitly warns 'Decide within 7 days of the leave date') — will have status:'approved' in leavedesk_v3 but its date-key is < rc, so produce() skips it and no LEAVE_APPROVED event is ever emitted. consumeAttendanceFeed() therefore never buckets it into saagar_payroll_attendance_feed.
impact: That approved absence silently never appears in the payroll attendance feed for the affected employee/month, so the payroll maker can over-pay (counts a present day where the employee was on approved leave). This is an owner-facing figure gap. It is documented in the UI note, so it is a known limitation rather than a silent defect, hence P2 not P0.
fix_hint: No safe fix inside leave.html alone (the window lives in the bridge, and RECENT_DAYS bounding is deliberate to avoid re-flooding the bus). Best module-side mitigation: surface the constraint at decision time — when decideLeave() approves a leave whose key is older than ~7 days, show a warning toast that it will not auto-sync to payroll and must be entered manually. Any change to the bridge scan window is out of scope for this read-only leave audit and must not touch storage-core.
evidence: integration-bridge.js line 136 skips `dk<rc`; line 137-139 only emits for `l.status==='approved'` (or legacy no-status). Node: cutoffIso(7) on 2026-07-03 = 2026-06-26, so any leave dated <=2026-06-25 is skipped.

title: Bridge-seeded staff show 'No ID' in Staff Master due to employeeId vs empId field-name mismatch
location: leave.html renderEmpList() line 2033 reads emp.empId; addEmployee() line 2076 writes empId; integration-bridge.js reconcileMasters() line 550 writes employeeId
description: When the bridge auto-seeds the central Employee Master into Leave's data.employees, it creates records shaped {id, name, employeeId:e.empId||'', department:e.dept||''} (bridge line 550). Leave's own addEmployee() instead stores the ID under empId (line 2076), and renderEmpList() reads emp.empId (line 2033) for display. title: getInitials()/getAvatarColor() throw on a leave or employee row with a missing name
location: getAvatarColor() line 1136-1137 (name.length/charCodeAt) and getInitials() line 1141-1142 (name.split); callers renderCalendar() line 1532, openDayModal() line 1538, renderEmpList() line 2023
description: getAvatarColor() dereferences name.length/name.charCodeAt and getInitials() calls name.split(' ') with no null guard. In-app writers always supply a name and importJSON() rejects rows with empty name, so this is only reachable via a corrupt/hand-edited leavedesk_v3 blob containing a leave/employee whose name is missing or non-string. Such a row makes renderCalendar() throw at getAvatarColor(l.name) (line 1532), breaking the whole grid render.
impact: A single malformed stored row (name undefined) crashes calendar rendering — module goes blank. Low likelihood because normal write paths guarantee name; only corrupt storage triggers it.
fix_hint: Guard both helpers: `function getInitials(name){name=String(name||'');...}` and `function getAvatarColor(name){name=String(name||'?');...}`. Additive, no storage-core change.

title: Multi-day leave collapses to 1 day unless duplicated under every date-key
location: saagar-report.js:582-591 (leaveRegister builder)
description: Leave-day counting relies on the SAME leave object appearing once under each calendar day-key in leavedesk_v3.leaves. The dedup key is name|leaveFrom|leaveTo|type; the FIRST occurrence creates rec.days=1, every subsequent day-key that repeats the same object does seen[key].days++. So a 3-day leave is only counted as 3 days IF the store writes it under all 3 date-keys. If leavedesk stores a span-leave ONCE (under leaveFrom only) with leaveFrom≠leaveTo, days stays 1 and the Leave-Days column + payroll KPI undercount the actual span. There is no from/to date-diff fallback to derive the true span, so the register silently disagrees with the roster.
impact: Payroll-facing leave-day totals can be materially wrong (a week-long leave shown as 1 day), understating deductions the owner relies on. Whether it triggers depends entirely on the leavedesk write pattern — needs runtime confirmation of how spans are persisted.
fix_hint: When l.leaveFrom and l.leaveTo differ, compute inclusive day-span from the two ISO dates (local-midnight, floor) and use that as rec.days instead of the ++ counter; keep the ++ path only as a fallback for stores that do duplicate per-day. Additive logic in the builder only — no storage change.

title: GST invoice CGST+SGST halves can display 1 rupee more/less than Total GST
location: saagar-report.js:821, 841-845
description: gstAmt = sub*gstPct/100. CGST and SGST are each printed as inr(gstAmt/2), i.e. Math.round(gstAmt/2) TWICE and independently. When gstAmt is an odd rupee amount (e.g. 101), inr(50.5) rounds to ₹51 for BOTH halves → CGST+SGST shown = ₹102, while 'Total GST' printed as inr(gstAmt)=inr(101)=₹101 and 'Total Payable'=sub+gstAmt=₹101. The two halves shown on the tax invoice do not sum to the Total GST / Total Payable shown on the same invoice.
impact: A legal GST tax invoice can show internally inconsistent tax figures (halves sum ≠ total) by ±1 rupee. Small in value but it is a wrong money figure on a document handed to a customer / used for filing.
fix_hint: Round one half and derive the other by subtraction: cgst = Math.round(gstAmt/2); sgst = Math.round(gstAmt) - cgst; then show inr(cgst)/inr(sgst) and Total GST = inr(cgst+sgst). No new libs, builder-only.

title: Invoice Total Payable can use owner-entered finalAmt that doesn't reconcile with taxable+GST shown
location: saagar-report.js:822, 843-845
description: finalAmt = parseFloat(del.finalAmt) || (sub + gstAmt). If del.finalAmt is present but was entered/rounded to a value other than sub+gstAmt (e.g. rounded-off collection, or entered before GST%), the invoice prints Taxable Value (sub), Total GST (gstAmt) and a Total Payable (finalAmt) that do not add up. There is no guard that finalAmt ≈ sub+gstAmt.
impact: Tax invoice may show Taxable + GST ≠ Total Payable, an arithmetic inconsistency on a GST document. Depends on whether del.finalAmt is ever set independently of sub/gst — needs runtime confirmation of the delivery flow.
fix_hint: Either always compute finalAmt = sub+gstAmt for the invoice, or when del.finalAmt differs by >₹1 add a rounding-adjustment line so the components reconcile to the printed total. Builder-only.

title: Negative currency renders as '₹-500' (sign after the rupee symbol)
location: saagar-report.js:16 (inr), used at 150/193/219 (variance), 693/860/873/879 (surplus/net P&L)
description: inr(n) = '₹' + Math.round(n).toLocaleString('en-IN'). For negatives toLocaleString yields '-500', so output is '₹-500' instead of '-₹500'. Appears wherever a shortfall/loss is shown: cash variance when short, Net P&L loss, operating surplus deficit, KPI negative subs.
impact: Cosmetic on money the owner sees — the figure and its magnitude are correct, only the minus/symbol order is non-standard. Not a wrong value, but reads oddly on cash-mismatch and loss lines.
fix_hint: In inr(), format the absolute value and prefix the sign: var v=Math.round(Number(n)||0); return (v<0?'-':'')+'₹'+Math.abs(v).toLocaleString('en-IN'); Single-line change, no behaviour change for positives.

title: Brought/Carried-forward lines skipped when the final page holds only the foot (or head) row
module: renderDoc carry-forward (payrollRegister, leaveRegister, dsr/qms bill tables)
location: saagar-report.js:1153-1164 (drawCarryAfter) + 1176-1182 (didDrawCell page tracking)
description: carry.pageRows is populated only from didDrawCell where d.section==='body'. Page membership and rec.max/rec.min derive purely from body rows. If autoTable pushes the TOTAL (foot) row — or a repeated header — onto a fresh final page with no body rows on it, that page is absent from pageRows: no 'Brought forward' is drawn on it, yet the previous page still gets a 'Carried forward' equal to the grand total that then re-appears immediately as the foot TOTAL. Also, if a single body row is the only one on a trailing page, rec.min===rec.max and the brought/carried math still works, but the foot-only-page case produces a visually redundant/again-missing carry line.
impact: On large seeded datasets (366-day / many-employee registers) a page break landing right before the foot row yields a carried-forward line with no matching brought-forward on the last page — looks like a dropped continuation. Money totals in the foot remain correct; only the running-total furniture is off. Needs runtime repro with a body that fills to exactly the page boundary.
fix_hint: After autoTable, also seed pageRows for doc.lastAutoTable pages that only carry head/foot (use lastAutoTable.startPageNumber..finalY page span), or suppress the 'Carried forward' on the second-to-last page when the next page has no body rows. Renderer-only.

title: Payroll fallback OT is back-solved and can be silently wrong / hide sign errors
location: saagar-report.js:403, 441
description: In the localStorage fallback (shell Reports hub, no live opts.rows), overtime is derived as ot = Math.max(0, Math.round(net + pt + pf + esic + advance - gross)). This assumes net = gross + ot - (pt+pf+esic+advance) exactly. If the stored net was computed with any other component (rounding, special allowance, LOP already applied differently), the reconstructed OT absorbs the entire discrepancy, and the Math.max(0,...) clamps a negative residual to 0 — so Gross+OT and the OT column can misstate the earnings split while Net stays right. The live opts path (fromOpts) is exact; only the mirror path is affected.
impact: Salary register / slip built from the mirror (not opened live from payroll) can show an OT figure that is a plug rather than real overtime, misrepresenting the earnings breakdown to the owner. Net Pay stays correct. Depends on how faithfully net was mirrored — needs runtime check against a real payroll run.
fix_hint: Prefer a stored r.ot when present in the mirror; only back-solve when no OT field exists, and label the reconstructed value (e.g. footnote) so a clamped/negative residual is visible rather than silently zeroed. Builder-only, additive.

title: serviceAging table uses computeServiceAging KPI counts but its own recomputed open list — bucket vs row divergence possible
location: saagar-report.js:748-769
description: The KPI tiles (Total Open, 0-3/4-7/8-15/16+) come from G('computeServiceAging'), but the detail table re-derives the open set locally by filtering saagar_wsf_v2 on a hardcoded closedW word list and re-ages with local-midnight/floor. If computeServiceAging uses a different closed-status definition or different date field precedence than the local filter, the KPI '16+' count and the number of rows flagged j.__days>15 in the table can disagree, and Total Open (KPI) may not equal open.length (table).
impact: Owner sees a header count of open/aged cases that does not match the rows listed below it — erodes trust and can hide or invent a backlog case. Real divergence depends on computeServiceAging's internal rules — needs runtime comparison on seeded service data.
fix_hint: Drive both the KPI numbers and the table from ONE source: either surface computeServiceAging's own open list, or compute buckets locally from the same filtered 'open' array used for the table. Builder-only.

title: cashDetail expected-closing ignores non-cash opening and never validates counted vs bank+drawer
location: saagar-report.js:49-53, 216-220
description: expected = opening + cashIn - cashOut, variance = counted - expected. Separately 'Retained in drawer' = inr(counted - bankDep). There is no cross-check that counted == bankDep + retained, and denoTotal silently coerces non-numeric denomination counts via Number(map[d])||0 (a stray string denom count becomes 0). So a corrupted physDeno/bankDeno entry quietly drops cash from the counted/deposited totals without flagging, changing the variance the owner reconciles against.
impact: A single malformed denomination value silently understates counted cash and can turn a balanced day into an apparent shortage (or mask a real one). Requires a non-numeric denom value in storage to trigger — low likelihood but it is the owner's cash-reconciliation figure.
fix_hint: In denoTotal, distinguish missing (0) from non-numeric (NaN) and surface a 'denomination data unreadable' note; add an assert that bankDep ≤ counted and show a warning when counted-bankDep is negative. Builder/helper-only, no storage write.

title: Font-embedding failure throws late (per-render) rather than degrading — a missing DMSans blanks every report
location: saagar-report.js:972-977, 1226
description: setFonts() throws 'DMSans normal+bold not registered' if either weight is missing. renderDoc calls it after constructing the doc; the throw propagates to build()/generate()/preview() which only toast('Could not build report'). Offline, if fonts/DMSans-normal.js or -bold.js fails to load, NO report renders at all (hard fail) and the only signal is a transient toast — there is no fallback to a core PDF font, so the rupee glyph requirement takes the whole engine down.
impact: A single missing/failed font asset in the offline bundle disables the entire report engine (all 20 report types) with only a toast, not a partial or plain-font PDF. Depends on asset-load reliability in the packaged APK — needs runtime confirmation the two font JS files always register.
fix_hint: This is by-design (rupee correctness) but the failure is silent; keep the throw yet ensure the build gate that loads the fonts surfaces a persistent, explicit 'reports unavailable — font not loaded' state rather than a transient toast, and verify both font files are in the offline manifest. No code path should invent a substitute rupee.

title: trunc() truncation can garble the last visible characters and drops width-0 guard
location: saagar-report.js:1139
description: trunc(s,n) returns s.slice(0, n-2)+'...' when s.length>n. For very small n (n<=2) n-2 is <=0, so slice(0,0)+'...' yields just '...', losing the value entirely; and it counts JS string length, so a multi-codepoint name is cut mid-grapheme. Column truncation widths in builders are all comfortably >2 so the '...'-only case isn't hit today, but any future narrow column (n<=2) would silently blank the cell.
impact: No current wrong-data case (all call sites use n>=12); purely a latent trap for narrow columns and combining-character names. Trivial.
fix_hint: Guard: if (n<=1) return s.slice(0,n); use Math.max(0,n-1)+'…' or keep at least one real char before the ellipsis. Helper-only.

title: Restore rejects saagar_invoice_seq_v1 (a plain number) because the service validator demands an array — counter is dropped, new/restored device reissues DUPLICATE invoice numbers
location: index.html:5213 (validateRestoreKeyValue owner==='service') vs storage value written at service module ~line 3625 as String(seq)
description: saagar_invoice_seq_v1 is stored as a BARE integer string (e.g. "42"), confirmed by the project's own audit evidence: `let seq = parseInt(localStorage.getItem('saagar_invoice_seq_v1')||'0',10); ... c.invoiceNo='WS-'+year+'-'+String(seq).padStart(3,'0')`. It IS in STORAGE_RULES.service.exact so it exports fine. But on restore, restoreKeyOwnerId returns 'service' (not 'control', so the control-key bypass at 5205-5210 does not apply), and validateRestoreKeyValue line 5213 does `return {ok:Array.isArray(parsed)}` for ALL service keys. parsedRestoreValue("42")=42, Array.isArray(42)=false -> {ok:false} -> pushed to result.invalid -> the key is NOT written back. The round-trip silently drops the invoice counter.
impact: After a restore or full migration to a new phone, the invoice sequence resets to '0'. The service module then reissues WS-<year>-001, 002... that collide with invoice numbers already printed on delivered customer job cards/proformas. Duplicate customer-facing invoice numbers = billing/audit integrity break; the owner has no signal it happened. This is exactly the additive-key-dropped class the task flagged.
fix_hint: In validateRestoreKeyValue, exempt the two non-array service keys before the array check: `if(owner==='service' && (k==='saagar_invoice_seq_v1'||k==='saagar_wsf_settings_v1')) return {ok:true};` (mirrors the existing gm_role exemption at 5211). Keep the array rule only for saagar_wsf_v2 (the case list). Validator-only change; no storage-core edit, no new key, additive.

title: Restore also rejects saagar_wsf_settings_v1 (an object) under the same 'service must be array' rule — the watch-photo-mandatory policy silently reverts to default on restore
location: index.html:5213; key documented in SCHEMA.md:247/464 as object {watchPhotoMandatory:bool}
description: saagar_wsf_settings_v1 is a single-blob OBJECT ({watchPhotoMandatory:bool}) per the project's own SCHEMA.md ('array · object' — it is the object). It sits in STORAGE_RULES.service.exact, so owner==='service' and it hits the same line 5213 Array.isArray gate. An object fails Array.isArray -> {ok:false} -> result.invalid -> dropped on restore. Same root cause as finding 1: the service validator was written when saagar_wsf_v2 was the only service key and never updated when Wave-2/3 added two non-array service keys.
impact: On restore/migration the admin policy 'a case cannot be saved without a received-condition watch photo' is lost and falls back to default, weakening the evidence-capture control the owner deliberately enabled. Silent — no rejected-key surfacing beyond a count.
fix_hint: Covered by the same fix as finding 1 (exempt saagar_wsf_settings_v1 from the array rule). Alternatively broaden line 5213 to accept an object for settings and array for the case list. Validator-only, additive.

title: saagar_bridge_config is not in the backup whitelist — owner-tuned integration thresholds (voucher ₹, fail %, leave gates) are dropped from every backup/restore/migration
location: index.html STORAGE_RULES 1923-1935 + appControlKeys 2070 (neither covers it); written integration-bridge.js:42 CFG='saagar_bridge_config', read/used line 492 voucherThreshold
description: saagar_bridge_config is the SOLE persistence for the integration rules {failPct, voucherThreshold(default 2000), leaveGates}. It starts with 'saagar_' but matches NO STORAGE_RULES exact/prefix (the only saagar_ prefixes are saagar_stock_/saagar_dsr_/saagar_grooming_) and is NOT in appControlKeys, so isWhitelistedAppKey('saagar_bridge_config') is false. appStorage() filters by isWhitelistedAppKey, so the key is excluded from backupPayload, migration export, AND the pre-factory-reset safety backup. integration-bridge.js line 492 uses voucherThreshold to gate voucher creation.
impact: After restore or a full migration to the new system, the owner's tuned business rules silently revert to defaults (voucher approval threshold back to ₹2000, fail% back to 60, leave gates re-enabled). No warning. Not a wrong-money-figure, but a silently-lost owner configuration that drives an approval workflow — the 'check for more dropped additive keys' the task asked for.
fix_hint: Add 'saagar_bridge_config' to appControlKeys() (it is app-control state, not a module blob), OR give it its own STORAGE_RULES entry. Then also add a restore validator branch (owner==='control' -> {ok:true} already covers it once whitelisted, since it is not one of the specially-validated control keys). Additive, no storage-core edit.

title: Restore rollback snapshot ignores safeSet failure — a large (3327-key) backup can exceed quota, the rollback is silently NOT saved, then data is overwritten with no undo
location: index.html:5285 safeSet(rollbackKey,...) return ignored; overwrite proceeds at 5290
description: restoreValidatedBackup builds a rollback object holding the PRIOR value of every key being restored, then `safeSet(rollbackKey, JSON.stringify(rollback))` at 5285. safeSet returns false on QuotaExceededError (2064) but the return is discarded. Immediately after, line 5290 overwrites all keys. For a full restore of thousands of keys, the rollback blob roughly DOUBLES the footprint of the restored data at the moment of writing, so on a near-full store the rollback write is the most likely thing to fail — precisely when the user most needs undo. The UI promised 'A rollback snapshot will be saved before any data is replaced' (5258).
impact: On a large restore near quota, the rollback silently does not persist, then the overwrite runs anyway. If the restored file was wrong/partial, the owner cannot undo — the promised safety net is absent exactly in the large-snapshot case the task called out. No corruption of the restored data itself, hence P2, but it breaks the stated safety guarantee.
fix_hint: Check the safeSet return: `if(!safeSet(rollbackKey, JSON.stringify(rollback))){ if(!confirm('Could not save an undo snapshot (storage full). Restore without the ability to undo?')) { closeModal(); return; } }`. Message must be English. Additive; no storage-core edit.

title: ui_day_closed / ui_hide_amounts / saagar_selected_date / saagar_acting_as / saagar_ui_mode are excluded from backup by the whitelist (benign, but confirms the manifest's 'every key' claim is inaccurate)
location: index.html EOD_CLOSED_KEY 2920, ui_hide_amounts 3012, SELECTED_DATE_KEY 2022, ACTING_AS_KEY 2861, UI_MODE_KEY 6681; whitelist 1923-2072
description: These persisted keys are not in STORAGE_RULES nor appControlKeys, so isWhitelistedAppKey drops them from backup/migration. Unlike findings 1-3 the lost state is ephemeral UI/session (today's EOD tick, amount-hide toggle, viewed date, acting-as impersonation, mobile/desktop layout) and self-heals, so losing it on restore is acceptable — arguably correct (you would not want a stale ui_day_closed or saagar_acting_as to travel to a new phone). Flagged only because the migration manifest text/comments imply a complete key set ('EVERY storage key', keyInventory over 'totalKeys') while these are silently outside the count, and because it documents that the whitelist-only design is the mechanism that also caused finding 3.
impact: No data loss of business value. Cosmetic reset of preferences after restore. Manifest key inventory undercounts device state, which a rebuild importer should be aware of.
fix_hint: No code change required for the ui_*/session keys (dropping them is desirable). If exhaustive fidelity is wanted for the layout preference only, add saagar_ui_mode to appControlKeys. Otherwise document in the manifest that ephemeral ui_*/session keys are intentionally excluded.

title: Admin session flag is a plaintext localStorage boolean — staff can self-promote to owner without the PIN
location: www/index.html:2134 (setAdmin), 6733 (boot restore), 1938 (ADMIN_MODE_KEY)
description: Admin/owner mode is gated only by the in-memory flag `isAdmin`, which is persisted verbatim as the string 'true' under localStorage key st_v2_admin_mode (setAdmin, line 2134) and re-read on every boot (line 6733: `isAdmin = safeGet(ADMIN_MODE_KEY)==='true'`). The PIN check in unlockAdmin (2149) is the ONLY thing that normally flips this flag, but nothing binds the persisted flag back to the PIN. Concrete bypass on a shared shop device: a staff member opens the app's WebView in a debuggable build / connected browser devtools / or any file-manager that can reach the app's localStorage, runs `localStorage.setItem('st_v2_admin_mode','true')` (or, in the app, evaluates `setAdmin(true)`), reloads, and is now owner — payroll, tax, backup, restore, wipe, role editor all unlocked, PIN never entered. `isAdmin===true` makes ensureModuleAccess (2174) and roleCanOpen (1991) return true unconditionally. This is the highest-leverage weakness: it defeats the PIN entirely without ever attacking the hash.
impact: On a shared owner/staff device a curious or malicious staffer gains full owner access (payroll salaries, tax figures, delete/restore/wipe of all data) by setting one localStorage string, with no PIN. Realistic on a debuggable APK or if the device WebView is inspectable. Does not require cracking the hash.
fix_hint: Do not trust a standalone persisted admin-mode boolean. Additive-localStorage fix: on boot, only honor st_v2_admin_mode==='true' if a companion token derived from the current PIN hash also matches — e.g. store alongside it a value `simpleHash(pin_hash + 'admin-session-v1')` and recompute+compare from st_v2_admin_pin_hash at boot; if it doesn't match, force isAdmin=false. This ties the session flag to knowledge of the PIN without new libs. (Cannot make it truly tamper-proof in an offline WebView, but raises it well above a one-word edit.) Better still, do not persist admin mode across launches at all — default isAdmin=false every boot so a staffer can't leave it unlocked. Obeys hard rules; no storage-core edits.

title: PIN hash is a fast 32-bit non-cryptographic hash with no salt and no attempt throttling — trivially brute-forced offline
location: www/index.html:2091 (simpleHash), 2142 (store), 2148-2149 (verify)
description: The PIN is stored as simpleHash(pin) (line 2142), where simpleHash (2091) is an unsalted FNV-1a-style function collapsing input to a 32-bit value rendered as a <=10-digit decimal string. It is not a KDF, not salted, and reversible-by-search: a 4-digit numeric PIN (the enforced minimum is only length>=4, and shop staff overwhelmingly pick 4-6 digit PINs) has 10k candidates; simpleHash over all of them takes microseconds. Given read access to st_v2_admin_pin_hash (same device, same localStorage as SEC-PIN-01), an attacker recovers the actual PIN by brute force, then enters it normally so no tampering is visible. Additionally unlockAdmin (2148) has NO attempt counter, delay, or lockout (confirmed: no throttle/lockout code exists), so even blind on-device guessing of a 4-digit PIN is feasible by hand and instant by script. The 32-bit space also admits collisions, but brute-forcing the small PIN space is the practical attack.
impact: Anyone who can read the stored hash (trivial on this device — plaintext localStorage) recovers the owner PIN, defeating payroll/tax protection and any future PIN-gated action. No lockout means even naive repeated guessing is unpunished.
fix_hint: Within hard rules (no new libs / offline): (a) strengthen the stored hash to a slow, salted, many-round construction built only from simpleHash — e.g. generate a random per-device salt (crypto.getRandomValues), store it, and store simpleHash iterated N thousand times over salt+pin; verify the same way. This kills precomputation and slows brute force. (b) Add an attempt counter in localStorage: after e.g. 5 wrong PINs impose an escalating delay / disable unlock for a cooldown window, so hand-guessing a 4-digit PIN is not instant. (c) Consider requiring 6+ digits. All additive-localStorage, no storage-core touch. Note: on an offline device a determined attacker with the hash can still brute force eventually — the goal here is raising cost above 'microseconds and no lockout'.

title: Protected-module data is only navigation-gated, not withheld — payroll/tax figures are readable from plaintext localStorage regardless of PIN or role

The honest, in-scope fix is expectation-setting: reword the protection copy (e.g. Settings 'Require admin PIN…' description near line 1493 and the toast at 2178) to state it restricts the in-app view only and is not encryption, so the owner does not overtrust it. title: Restore accepts an attacker-supplied admin PIN hash and admin-mode flag from a backup file — tampered migration file can preset owner access or swap the PIN
location: www/index.html:5206 (validateRestoreKeyValue control-keys), 2070 (appControlKeys export list)
description: The audit's own threat model includes 'tampered backup/migration file from another device'. appControlKeys (2070) exports/imports ADMIN_PIN_KEY and ADMIN_MODE_KEY, and validateRestoreKeyValue (5206) explicitly returns {ok:true} for ADMIN_PIN_KEY, ADMIN_MODE_KEY and PROTECTED_MODULES_KEY with no content check. So a backup/migration JSON crafted on another device can carry st_v2_admin_mode='true' (device boots already-owner, SEC-PIN-01) and/or st_v2_admin_pin_hash set to simpleHash of a PIN the attacker knows, and/or st_v2_protect_admin_modules='false' (disables payroll/tax gating outright). Concrete attack: attacker hands the shop a 'migration file' (a supported flow per the memory notes); after restore, the attacker's PIN is the device PIN, or protection is off, or admin is pre-unlocked — the legitimate owner is unaware their PIN was replaced. Because the restore validator waves these control keys through, the tampered file needs no special format.

Directly in the stated threat model (tampered file from another device).
fix_hint: Additive, no-storage-core: exclude the auth control keys (ADMIN_PIN_KEY, ADMIN_MODE_KEY, PROTECTED_MODULES_KEY) from RESTORE — restore should never import someone else's PIN hash or unlock state. Keep them exportable for the owner's own device migration only behind a confirm, but on import either (a) skip them entirely and preserve the current device's PIN, or (b) require re-entering the CURRENT device PIN before allowing these three keys to be overwritten. title: First-run 'set a PIN' is opportunistic, so a fresh/never-configured device grants owner access on first unlock tap with a self-chosen PIN

On a device where the owner never set a PIN (default state — hasAdminPin false), the FIRST person to tap 'Unlock admin' — which may be a staffer, not the owner — sets the PIN to a value THEY choose and becomes owner. There is no distinction between 'owner initializing' and 'staffer squatting'. Combined with the shared-device model this is a real land-grab: whoever gets there first owns the device auth. title: Role switch is unauthenticated — any staffer can select 'Store Manager' (all-modules) from the role picker with no PIN

description: The per-device role lives in localStorage key saagar_current_role_v1 and is changed by setCurrentRole (1990), which is wired to the role <select> in Settings (populated at 5634 / 2132). Additive change in setCurrentRole (1990) and the select's onchange wiring; no storage-core touch. Also consider that a device-wide 'current role' is inherently weak when staff share one device — document that roles are a convenience filter, not a security boundary.

title: changeAdminPin does not re-verify when already unlocked, so a left-unlocked session lets a passerby silently reset the owner PIN
location: www/index.html:2156-2163 (changeAdminPin)
description: changeAdminPin (2156) only asks for the CURRENT PIN inside the `if(!isAdmin)` unlock path; when isAdmin is already true it skips straight past the old-PIN check to promptNewPin (2163). Because admin mode persists across launches (SEC-PIN-01) and there is no auto-lock/timeout, the common shop scenario is: owner unlocks admin, walks away, leaves the app; a staffer opens Settings -> Change PIN and, since isAdmin is still true, is NOT asked for the old PIN and can set a new one they know — hijacking the owner's admin. Line 2159's `if(old){...}` guard is unreachable while already-admin because that branch is inside the earlier no-isAdmin block flow only when unlock was needed; when already admin it drops through to promptNewPin without ever comparing `old`.

fix_hint: Always require the CURRENT PIN before setting a new one, even when isAdmin is already true — move the old-PIN verification (2159-2162) so it runs unconditionally when an admin PIN exists. Also add an auto-lock: clear isAdmin after N minutes idle or on app background so a walked-away session cannot be abused. Both additive; no storage-core changes.

title: Restore rollback snapshot write is unchecked — quota failure leaves a destructive overwrite with NO undo

description: restoreValidatedBackup() takes the pre-restore rollback by building a full JSON of the current values of every key about to be overwritten and calling safeSet(rollbackKey, JSON.stringify(rollback)) at line 5285. Its return value is DISCARDED. safeSet (line 2064) catches QuotaExceededError, shows a toast, and returns false WITHOUT throwing. localStorage is a fixed ~5-10MB budget shared across all app keys; when the device is already near full (exactly the scenario a large restore aggravates) the rollback write silently fails. Execution then falls straight through to the bulk overwrite loop (line 5290) which replaces the live keys anyway. The advertised 'A rollback snapshot will be saved before any data is replaced' (line 5258) is therefore a false promise on a full device.

If the imported file is wrong/stale, the pre-restore data is unrecoverable from within the app. Silent partial/total loss.

title: Restore is additive-merge with no pre-clear — a mid-import failure or a partial backup leaves inconsistent cross-module state
location: www/index.html:5279-5291 (restoreValidatedBackup), 5222-5233 (validateRestoreData)
description: restoreValidatedBackup() writes only the keys present-and-valid in the imported file (Object.keys(review.valid)) and NEVER clears keys that exist on-device but are absent from the backup. It is a key-by-key overwrite inside SaagarStore.bulk() (line 5291). Two integrity consequences: (1) NON-ATOMIC vs. the live DB — validation runs before the write, but if a mid-loop safeSet throws for one key (e.g. a single oversized value or a transient quota edge) subsequent keys silently do not get written (written++ only increments on success, no rollback is triggered), leaving a half-restored mix of old and new keys across modules. (2) MERGE-not-replace — restoring an OLDER or module-partial backup onto a device that has newer data for other modules yields a Frankenstein state: e.g. restored stock/service rows keyed to employees or customers that the (older) EMP_MASTER/CUST_MASTER in the same file references, mixed with day-keys the backup never touched. Referential consistency across modules (employee IDs, store keys, udhaar↔customer) is not enforced on import.

No transaction wraps the whole restore, so there is no all-or-nothing guarantee; the rollback key (see SEC-DATA-01) is the only recovery and it can silently be absent.
fix_hint: Additive: after the bulk write, compare written vs keys.length; if written<keys.length, surface a hard warning and offer the rollback key immediately rather than reloading into a mixed state. Consider gating restore on payload.version/apkBuild compatibility (already present in payload) and warning when the file predates on-device data. No pre-clear change needed to satisfy the additive-only rule.

combo: restore a stale/partial or oversized backup

title: No size/shape guard on imported backup — a huge or deeply nested JSON can OOM/freeze the WebView during parse or double the footprint via the rollback
location: www/index.html:5234-5277 (handleRestoreFile), 5279-5285 (rollback build)
description: handleRestoreFile() does reader.readAsText then JSON.parse(reader.result) (line 5240) with no size cap and no streaming. A hostile or accidentally-huge file (the migration export itself can be MBs with embedded photos/evidence as base64) is fully materialized as a string, parsed to an object, re-validated (each value re-stringified at line 5226 for non-string values), then on apply a SECOND full copy is built for the rollback (line 5283-5284) and written back into the same localStorage budget. Peak memory is several multiples of the file size, and the whole thing runs on the main thread (no worker), freezing the UI. JSON.parse is in try/catch so it cannot crash-loop, and WAL replay (storage-core.js:146-159) wraps every op in try/catch and never JSON-parses stored values — so a bad restored value cannot throw on every boot. The realistic worst case is a hang / quota-exceeded toast, not an unrecoverable crash-loop.

Bounded (no persistent corruption) because parse and replay are both guarded.
fix_hint: Additive: reject files above a sane byte threshold (e.g. warn >8MB) before JSON.parse, and cap/skip the rollback copy for very large payloads with an explicit 'no rollback for this size — export current data first' prompt. No new libs.
evidence: 5240 JSON.parse(reader.result) unbounded; 5283-5284 second full copy for rollback into same LS budget; storage-core.js:151-158 replay try/catch per op, values kept as strings (no boot crash-loop).
combo: import a multi-MB migration/photo backup on a low-RAM device

title: Shell postMessage handler validates neither event.origin nor event.source (no allowlist)
location: saagar-control-centre/www/index.html:6479-6492
description: window.addEventListener('message', ...) dispatches ST_BACK_HOME, ST_OPEN_MODULE, ST_PRINT, ST_REPORT, ST_REPORT_BATCH, ST_SHARE, ST_WA and ST_AUDIT purely on e.data.type, with NO check of e.origin or e.source. Any window that can obtain a handle to the shell window could post a forged ST_* event. In principle this lets a foreign context trigger navigation, open a print/preview host, kick off report generation, or write audit-log entries.
impact: Defense-in-depth gap only under the shipped threat model. The app is a packaged offline APK with the INTERNET permission removed (build-apk.yml:48-49), so no remote/foreign page can ever load, and the sole real sender (#moduleFrame) is a non-sandboxed srcdoc iframe that is ALREADY same-origin (index.html:1634, 5752) with full parent.document access — so forging ST_* buys an attacker nothing they don't already have. There is no offline path for untrusted script to reach this listener. Real exploitability: effectively nil in this build; the risk would only materialise if a future build re-adds INTERNET, loads any remote content, opens an attacker-controllable window, or sandboxes the module frame to a null origin. Worth hardening now because the handler is the shell's single cross-frame trust seam.
fix_hint: Additive guard at the top of the listener (no libraries, no storage-core touch): (1) accept only messages whose e.source === document.getElementById('moduleFrame').contentWindow (the one legitimate sender); (2) additionally gate on e.origin being the app origin (location.origin, i.e. https://localhost) OR the empty-string/'null' that same-origin srcdoc posts — test on-device since srcdoc origin reporting varies; (3) whitelist e.data.type against the known ST_* set and early-return otherwise. This preserves every current flow (all legit posts come from that frame) while closing the seam if the environment ever changes.

Sender frame confirmed non-sandboxed same-origin: iframe#moduleFrame declared at 1634 with no sandbox attr; grep for `sandbox` in index.html returns only the prose comment at 5752.

location: saagar-control-centre/www/index.html:6519-6551 (stPrintBridge), dispatched at 6483
description: stPrintBridge takes e.data.html and e.data.css straight from the posted message and injects them into #st-print-host via host.innerHTML = ... + (data.css?'<style>'+data.css+'</style>':'') + (data.html||'') + ... . This host lives in the TOP document (not the iframe), is shown fullscreen (html.st-preview-open), and its content is later rasterised to PDF and can be printed. The HTML/CSS are inserted with zero sanitisation, so a forged or malicious ST_PRINT can place arbitrary markup (and, via the injected <style>, arbitrary CSS) into the shell's own document.
impact: This is the sharpest item on the bus because it moves attacker-shaped content OUT of the sandbox-less-but-still-iframe module and INTO the top document, and inline event handlers / crafted CSS would execute/apply in the shell context. However, under the shipped offline threat model the only entity that can post ST_PRINT is a first-party bundled module already running same-origin (see pm-01 threat model) — such a module can already scribble on parent.document directly, so no privilege is actually gained. No offline breach; the concern is that IF the origin check (pm-01) is ever the only thing standing between a future untrusted sender and this sink, this is the sink that turns a forged message into top-document HTML/CSS injection. Note img/script-src can still trigger sub-resource loads, but INTERNET is stripped so they cannot exfiltrate.
fix_hint: Primarily fixed by pm-01 (only accept ST_PRINT from the module frame + type whitelist). As additional additive hardening without new libs: keep the injected <style> but wrap the print HTML build so it cannot introduce active content — e.g. strip on-* attributes and <script> from data.html with a small regex/DOM-parse-then-serialise pass before assigning innerHTML, or build into a detached document and import only element nodes. Do NOT add a sanitiser library (offline/no-new-libs rule) — a minimal inline scrub is sufficient given the same-origin-only sender.

' ...` ; host is #st-print-host appended to document.body at 6523; shown fullscreen top-level via html.st-preview-open (CSS 727). Reached from the unguarded handler at 6483 `if(e.data.type === 'ST_PRINT') stPrintBridge(e.data);`.

title: ST_AUDIT writes attacker-controlled action/detail/before/after into the audit log
location: saagar-control-centre/www/index.html:6488-6491 (dispatch) → auditLog 2098-2107
description: On ST_AUDIT the shell calls auditLog(e.data.action, e.data.detail||{}, e.data.before, e.data.after) with all four values taken verbatim from the posted message. auditLog unshifts the entry and persists JSON.stringify(log.slice(0,500)) to AUDIT_LOG_KEY. A forged ST_AUDIT can therefore inject arbitrary log entries (fake actions/actors-by-implication, bogus before/after blobs) or, by spamming, churn the 500-entry ring to evict genuine history.
impact: Integrity/pollution of the on-device audit trail only — no money figure changes, no crash, no data-file corruption (the log is a bounded additive localStorage array). Under the offline model the only sender is same-origin module code that could write AUDIT_LOG_KEY directly anyway, so no real escalation. Low blast radius; flagged for completeness because audit-log trustworthiness is a stated concern and this is the poisoning vector.
fix_hint: Covered by pm-01's source/type guard (only the module frame may post ST_AUDIT). Optionally, additively cap detail/before/after sizes and coerce action to a known-prefix string before logging so a single forged/oversized post can't bloat or evict the ring. No storage-core changes needed — auditLog already slices to 500.
evidence: index.html:6488 `if(e.data.type === 'ST_AUDIT' && e.data.action){ auditLog(e.data.action, e.data.detail||{}, e.data.before ?? null, e.data.after ?? null);` ; auditLog persists at 2106 `safeSet(AUDIT_LOG_KEY, JSON.stringify(log.slice(0,500)))`.

title: Distributed APK is a debug build — android:debuggable="true" ships to the owner's device
location: android/app/build/intermediates/merged_manifests/debug/AndroidManifest.xml:27 (debuggable injected); only debug variant exists — no release manifest under packaged_manifests/
description: The only build variant ever produced is the debug variant (only android/app/build/intermediates/{merged,packaged}_manifests/debug/ exist; no release/ dir). The debug build injects android:debuggable="true" into the application element, and the seeded distribution APK (SaagarCC-DemoData-V6-Wave3.apk per memory) is this debug artifact. A debuggable APK lets anyone with USB/adb access run `run-as com.saagartraders.bcc` and read the app's entire private data dir — including the primary SQLite business DB (sales, udhaar/credit ledger, payroll, GST figures) and the daily auto-backup — without root. It also allows attaching a JS/Java debugger to the live WebView.
impact: On a lost, stolen, serviced, or briefly borrowed phone, all of the shop owner's financial and customer data is trivially extractable via adb with no root and no PIN bypass. Debuggable production builds are a well-known OWASP MASVS failure (RESILIENCE).
fix_hint: Ship a RELEASE build, not debug. Build via the existing `npm run build:release` (cap sync + gradlew assembleRelease) and distribute that signed APK instead of assembleDebug output. Release builds do not inject debuggable. No source/manifest edit required — this is a build-process fix. Do NOT hand-add android:debuggable="false" to the source manifest as a substitute; use the release variant. Obeys all hard rules (build-only, no libs, offline).

title: android:allowBackup="true" permits adb-backup exfiltration of the offline SQLite business/financial data
location: android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:5 (android:allowBackup="true"); carried into merged/packaged manifest line 25
description: The application declares android:allowBackup="true" (the AGP default). Combined with minSdkVersion 22, this means `adb backup -f out.ab com.saagartraders.bcc` can pull the app's private files — the sql.js-backed SQLite database and the daily auto-backup blobs stored in app-private storage — off the device onto any PC, for any build (debug or release), without root. For an app whose entire value is holding a retailer's confidential ledgers (cash, udhaar, payroll, GST), full-data backup export is a meaningful confidentiality weakness.
impact: Anyone with brief physical access and USB debugging (or a device where the owner enabled it) can exfiltrate the complete business dataset via a standard adb backup, defeating the 'offline = safe' assumption. No malware or root needed.
fix_hint: Set android:allowBackup="false" on the <application> element in android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (single attribute flip; app has no cloud-backup requirement — backups are handled internally via the daily auto-backup file the user controls). This is a manifest attribute change only: no new library, no storage-core/sqlite-store/photo-store edits, offline posture preserved. If finer control is later wanted, add a data-extraction/backup rules XML, but the simple false is sufficient and lowest-risk.

title: INTERNET permission requested but the app is fully offline (unnecessary attack surface)
location: android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:40 (<uses-permission android.permission.INTERNET/>)
description: The manifest declares android.permission.INTERNET, but a grep of the entire www payload (index.html, saagar-report.js) shows no fetch/XMLHttpRequest/WebSocket to any remote host. The only outbound interactions are tel: and https://wa.me/ links, which are OS-handled external intents (they launch the dialer / WhatsApp / browser) and do NOT require the app process itself to hold INTERNET. Capacitor serves the bundled www over the local https://localhost WebViewAssetLoader scheme, which also does not need INTERNET. Keeping INTERNET granted means that if any bundled JS were ever compromised (or a future dependency added), it could silently exfiltrate the local DB over the network — a capability the app otherwise does not need.
impact: Contradicts the app's advertised offline-only security model and leaves an exfiltration channel available to any injected/compromised script. Low immediate risk (no current code uses it), but it is free attack surface on an app holding sensitive financial data.
fix_hint: Remove the <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET"/> line from android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml and re-verify on-device that (a) the app UI loads (localhost asset loading is unaffected) and (b) tel:/wa.me share still launch external apps. If a regression appears (some Capacitor/WebView configurations want INTERNET for the localhost scheme on certain OEMs), restore it — hence P2 not P1. Manifest-only change, no libs, offline preserved.

title: FileProvider file_paths grants whole external-storage and cache roots ('path="."')
location: android/app/src/main/res/xml/file_paths.xml:3-4 (external-path name="my_images" path="." ; cache-path path=".")
description: The FileProvider path config exposes the root of external-files storage and the cache dir (path=".") rather than a narrow subfolder. The provider itself is android:exported="false" and only hands out content:// URIs via explicit grantUriPermission during the share flow, so this is not directly world-readable. However, scoping the provider to the entire external/cache root is broader than needed: any transient file the app writes there becomes eligible for a share-grant, widening the surface if a share intent is ever mis-targeted.
impact: Low. Not remotely exploitable and gated by exported=false + per-URI grants. It is a defense-in-depth / least-privilege gap rather than an active breach.
fix_hint: Narrow file_paths.xml to the specific subdirectory used for outbound report/PDF sharing (e.g. a dedicated <cache-path name="shared_reports" path="shared/"/>) instead of path=".". XML-only change, no code/libs/storage-core touched, offline preserved. Low priority — safe to defer.

title: Bundled pdf.js 3.11.174 is within the CVE-2024-4367 affected range but the vulnerable path is UNREACHABLE (informational)
location: www/pdf.min.js (apiVersion "3.11.174"); sole consumer saagar-report.js:1456-1458 getDocument({url}) fed by URL.createObjectURL(blob) at :1429
description: CVE-2024-4367 lets a crafted PDF execute arbitrary JS via a malicious FontMatrix when pdf.js < 4.2.0 renders it with isEvalSupported (default true); 3.11.174 is in range. Reachability was traced: the only getDocument() call site is saagar-report.js line 1456, whose input is a blob URL created at line 1429, and every caller passes a blob the app itself just generated in-process with jsPDF (renderDoc(...).output('blob')). The app never ingests an external PDF — it is fully offline and the single <input type=file> (index.html:1425) accepts application/json,.json only. There is no code path by which an attacker-controlled PDF reaches pdf.js, so the CVE is not exploitable in this app.
impact: None in practice given current code. Risk would only materialize if a future change added an 'open/import external PDF' feature that routed untrusted bytes into pdfjsLib.getDocument. Recorded so that constraint is not silently lost.
fix_hint: No action required now (do not add libraries or upgrade pdf.js as part of this read-only audit). Preserve the invariant: keep the file input JSON-only and never feed externally-sourced PDF bytes to pdfjsLib.getDocument. If an external-PDF viewer is ever added later, upgrade pdf.js to >= 4.2.0 or set isEvalSupported=false at that time. Informational finding.
